_README: Volunteer work projects - club workdays a hiker can see and join.
features/VOLUNTEERING.md Phase B (#760) is the design;
lib/work_projects.py validates this file and export_work_projects.py
bakes it into conditions/work_projects.json. A merged pull request over
reviewed_at is what releases rows, the same property every other build
input has (pipeline/DATA_RELEASES.md).
EDITED BY HAND, AS THE STOPGAP THE DESIGN NAMES: club admin tooling
(VOLUNTEERING.md Phase E) is where rows will come from eventually, and
a reviewed file 'does not scale past a handful of early-partner clubs,
and it does not have to'. Until a real club supplies real workdays,
`rows` stays EMPTY - maintainer decision 2026-08-20, recorded on #760:
no invented workday may reach a hiker, because a person driving to a
trailhead for an event nobody scheduled is this feature's own failure
mode, self-inflicted.
`ua_sample_rows` publish to the UA and dev environments ONLY
(features/DATA_ENVIRONMENTS.md), so the mechanism is rehearsable end to
end. They carry relative dates - starts_in_days/ends_in_days from bake
time - so UA's fourteen-day window always holds something, and their
titles start with '[Sample]' so nothing downstream can drop the label.
A production row's shape (all of it validated by lib/work_projects.py):
id             stable string, e.g. 'nynjtc:2026-09-12-bear-mtn'
club_name      the club's own name, as they write it
title          what the day is, in the club's words
description    optional - what to bring, where to meet
lat, lon       where (and/or `mile` on the NOBO axis)
mile           optional NOBO mile from Springer
starts_on      YYYY-MM-DD
ends_on        YYYY-MM-DD (same day for a single-day event)
status         upcoming | completed | cancelled (default upcoming)
capacity       optional positive integer - absent means 'no cap stated'
signup_mode    'contact' (in_app arrives with #762's backend)
signup_contact mailto:/tel:/https: - the club's own channel
Recurrence is deliberately unmodelled (VOLUNTEERING.md's open question):
a date range covers a single day and a weekend, and 'every third
Saturday' should be decided from what clubs actually run.
